human_scale_fact: The Coptic Church is the oldest continuously operating Christian institution in Africa — founded before Rome adopted Christianity, before the New Testament was fully assembled, before the Council of Nicaea defined the Christian creed. When Copts are persecuted in Egypt, they are being persecuted in the land their ancestors have called home for 5,000 years. Egypt's constitution guarantees freedom of religion but church construction requires presidential approval — a process that can take decades. There are governorates in Upper Egypt where there is not a single licensed church for hundreds of thousands of Christians.

human_scale_fact: Antioch — modern Antakya in Turkey — is where followers of Jesus were first called 'Christians.' The city was one of the greatest in the Roman Empire and the base for Paul's missionary journeys. The Patriarchate of Antioch, which oversees the Greek Orthodox and Syriac Orthodox churches of Syria and Lebanon, is one of the five original patriarchates of Christianity — older than the Roman Catholic Church's claims of supremacy, older than Constantinople, older than Islam by 600 years. The village of Maaloula, 50 km from Damascus, is one of the last places on earth where Western Aramaic — the language Jesus spoke — is still used in daily life. Al-Nusra Front fighters stormed it in 2013. Two senior bishops of the Greek Orthodox Church of Antioch were kidnapped in Aleppo in 2013. Their fate remains unknown.

human_scale_fact: The Ahwazi Arabs have lived in what is now called Khuzestan for over 2,500 years — Arab tribes are documented there since at least 542 BCE, and by 638 CE they were already so established that local Arab clans fought alongside the Islamic conquest forces as indigenous allies, not newcomers. For centuries the region was officially called Arabistan — 'Land of the Arabs' — named so by the Safavid Persian Empire itself in its own imperial records. In 1925 Reza Shah, modernizing Iran on a nationalist model, renamed it Khuzestan and launched systematic Arabization-in-reverse: Arabic banned from schools, Arab names changed to Persian, Arab tribal leaders removed from power. Khuzestan province today produces approximately 80% of Iran's oil and 60% of its natural gas. The Ahwazi Arab population lives without adequate drinking water — their rivers are diverted to Persian-majority provinces — while the ground beneath them funds the Iranian state. In 2021, photographs circulated of Ahwazi people drinking from muddy puddles in one of the most oil-rich regions on earth. The tomb of the Biblical prophet Daniel is in Susa (Shush) — in the Ahwazi heartland — one of the holiest Jewish sites in the world, located in a land whose Arab population Iran has been trying to erase for a century.
key_quote: They tell us we are Iranian. But they teach our children in Persian. They take our water. They take our oil. They give us nothing. And then they arrest us for saying so.

Some Ahwazi Arab activists have sought Israeli media attention and political recognition given Iran as a common adversary.
